function: Predicts the unit-modulus analog beamforming vector directly from pre-estimated CSI for multi-user near-field XL-MIMO, without a codebook, maximizing the average achievable rate (pp. 1, 5-7).
system: BS with a 256-antenna half-wavelength ULA serving K=3 single-antenna UEs in the near field, LoS channel, 50 GHz carrier; no RIS (pp. 3-4, 6).
method: CNN with convolution, pooling, upsampling blocks and a tanh phase output, trained label-free on the negative average achievable rate; Adam, offline training, online inference (pp. 6-7).
data_channel: Custom simulator: near-field LoS spherical-wave channel with free-space path loss, angles [-60,60] deg, distances [5,50] m; random 75%/25% train/test split of generated samples (pp. 4, 6-7).
test_conditions: Random 75%/25% split at N=256, 50 GHz, SNR -20 to 20 dB; Figs. 9, 12 vary carrier (30-60 GHz) and N (128-512), retraining not stated (pp. 7-10).
baselines: Non-learned: near-field hierarchical [15], far-field hierarchical [39], exhaustive search with cost limit 256 and unlimited [36]; learned: none, only a no-tanh ablation (p. 7).
metrics: Average achievable rate (bps/Hz) versus SNR, carrier frequency, distance, angle, and number of BS antennas; training and validation loss curves (pp. 7-10).
complexity: none; only a qualitative claim of reduced complexity (p. 2) and a training-cost limit of 256 for the exhaustive baseline (p. 7).
q1_support: p. 4: "the channel model between the n-th antenna unit and the UE is expressed by" a near-field LoS spherical-wave model with free-space path loss (Eq. 3); a custom simulator, with no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 7: "The data set is randomly divided into a 75% training set and a 25% test set" is a held-out part of the same data; p. 8: "at different carrier frequencies" (and Fig. 12 for antennas) are sweeps with no statement that the network is reused or retrained.
q3_support: p. 7: "The compared benchmarks are as follows" lists only non-learned schemes (near-field hierarchical, far-field hierarchical, exhaustive search); p. 7: "models without tanh layers exhibit pronounced overfitting" is an ablation of the proposed model, and the learned schemes [16], [17] cited on p. 1 are not compared.
q4_support: p. 2: "reduces computational complexity" is a qualitative claim; the only cost figure is p. 7: "training cost limit of 256" for the exhaustive baseline, a signaling overhead; no FLOPs, parameter count, runtime, or order is reported.
q5_support: p. 7: "We utilize Python as the programming language to construct the deep learning network model using the PyTorch framework" describes a custom simulation; no code or data link and no public dataset appear in the 11 pages.
notes: arXiv v2 preprint, 11 pages read in full. Area 3: the CNN outputs the beamforming vector from CSI without a codebook, so the function is beamforming. q2 is not met on the explicit-statement rule: Figs. 9 and 12 vary carrier frequency and antenna count, but the paper never says the trained network is reused or retrained (its input and output sizes depend on N, p. 6). q3: the learned beam-training schemes [16], [17] are cited (p. 1) but not compared; the no-tanh model is an ablation. q4: complexity is claimed qualitatively only.
